title: Mother finds daughter dead, femicide case shocks Campo Grande
seoTitle: Mother finds daughter dead, femicide shocks Campo Grande
subtitle: The discovery of Adriele dos Santos' body by her mother mobilizes police and raises alarm on violence against women.
excerpt: The tragic discovery of 34‑year‑old Adriele dos Santos' body by her own mother in Campo Grande mobilized authorities on Saturday (29).
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
A desperate search by a mother for her missing daughter ended in a tragic discovery that has mobilized authorities in Campo Grande. Adriele dos Santos, 34, was found dead by her mother on the afternoon of Saturday (29) in a house in the Santo Antônio neighborhood. The case is being treated initially as a possible femicide, generating great repercussion and making the topic “mother” one of the most searched.

The discovery of the body

The Military Police were called around 1 p.m., after the victim failed to show up for work. Unable to contact her daughter, Adriele's mother went to the residence on Rua Brasil Central. After climbing over the wall, she found Adriele lifeless on a sofa with a rope around her neck. Early reports indicate the victim showed signs of strangulation, and the cause of death was asphyxiation, according to Deputy Larissa Serpa of the 1st DEAM (Specialized Women’s Assistance Police Station).

Investigation of possible femicide

The case is being treated as a possible femicide, and the Civil Police of Mato Grosso do Sul are investigating the circumstances of the death. The Fire Department and the Criminal Forensics Unit were called to carry out the necessary procedures on site. A police officer estimated that the death may have occurred around 10 p.m. on Friday (28), more than 12 hours before the body was located. The forensic examination should help clarify the exact cause and the dynamics of the death.

The suspect and relationship context

Adriele's husband, identified as Aparecido de Sousa Doirado, 46, is the main suspect. He voluntarily presented himself at the Civil Police Station to give statements. The victim's mother told officers that Adriele was going through a separation process, and the relationship had been unstable for about four years, marked by break‑ups and reconciliations. Security cameras captured the man leaving the house in the morning accompanied by the couple's three‑year‑old son. The husband had told the victim's mother that Adriele had been taken to the Santa Casa, which contradicted the security footage.

Support and reporting channels against violence

Deputy Larissa Serpa reported that Adriele did not have an active protective order nor recent reports filed against the alleged perpetrator. For women experiencing violence, the Casa da Mulher Brasileira in Campo Grande is open 24 hours a day, including weekends, at Rua Brasília, s/n, Jardim Imá. The center offers services such as Public Defender, Public Prosecutor's Office, social and psychological assistance, and shelter.

There are also contact numbers for reports and support: 153 and 190 for emergencies. The Women's Assistance Center – 180 is a 24/7 phone line for reception, guidance and referral, though not for emergencies. Promuse also provides assistance via phone and WhatsApp (67) 99180‑0542. In cases of negligence or errors by the Civil Police, complaints can be filed with the Civil Police Ombudsman of MS at (67) 3314‑1896 or with GACEP (Special Group for External Police Activity Control) of the MPMS at (67) 3316‑2836, (67) 3316‑2837 and (67) 9321‑3931.

With information from G1, Campo Grande News, Midiamax.
